question: Why is psychological safety so important in healthcare team meetings?

options.A: It guarantees that every meeting will finish exactly on schedule
options.B: It eliminates the need for a formal meeting agenda
options.C: It prevents nurses from ever disagreeing with senior doctors
options.D: It encourages junior staff to speak up about patient safety concerns without fear

explanation: When staff feel safe from harsh judgment, even junior nurses can freely speak up about safety risks.

question: Which emotional challenge often happens when older adults experience major life losses?

options.A: Excessive hyperactivity and euphoria
options.B: Depression and social isolation
options.C: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
options.D: Bipolar mood swings during sleep

explanation: Well done. Retiring, losing friends or family, and moving around less can make older adults feel lonely and lead to depression.

question: What is the main goal of triage when a mass casualty happens?

options.A: Sending all injured persons immediately to the operating theatre
options.B: Ensuring every single patient receives equal amounts of time
options.C: Doing the greatest good for the greatest number of people
options.D: Treating the most critically ill patient before anyone else

explanation: Great thinking! When supplies and staff are limited, triage helps us save as many lives as possible by prioritizing resources wisely.

question: Which hormone is the main driver of sexual desire in men?

options.A: Melatonin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Testosterone
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: Spot on! Testosterone is the key hormone responsible for keeping the male libido and sexual drive ticking.

question: What is the main protective job of antioxidants found in fruits and vegetables?

options.A: Neutralizing unstable free radicals that damage cells
options.B: Acting as direct hormones to lower blood pressure
options.C: Speeding up the mechanical digestion of dietary fats
options.D: Providing the main structural foundation for muscle tissue

explanation: Correct! Antioxidants fight off unstable free radicals so they don't damage our cells and DNA.

question: Which layer of the skin is affected in a simple first-degree (superficial) burn?

options.A: Both epidermis and deep muscle
options.B: The epidermis only
options.C: The dermis and fat layer
options.D: Only the subcutaneous tissue

explanation: Great job! First-degree burns only touch the outer layer of skin (the epidermis), causing redness and mild pain without any blisters.

question: Which hospital team member is usually your go-to expert for helping a discharged patient find housing and food support?

options.A: The psychiatric social worker
options.B: The surgical floor pharmacist
options.C: The hospital laboratory technician
options.D: The institutional chief accountant

explanation: Spot on! Social workers are pros at connecting patients with community support, government programs, and welfare resources.

question: You are trying to calm an upset patient in their living room. Which action keeps everyone safe?

options.A: Touching the client's shoulder frequently to show physical warmth
options.B: Maintaining a safe distance and keeping the exit route clear
options.C: Raising the voice to ensure the client hears every single instruction
options.D: Standing directly in front of the doorway to block the client from leaving

explanation: Spot on! Giving personal space and making sure nobody feels trapped is a golden rule for safety during de-escalation.

question: Why is the left anterior descending (LAD) artery famously called the widow-maker?

options.A: It carries deoxygenated blood back to the lungs.
options.B: It is the longest vein in the human heart.
options.C: It supplies blood to the major pumping walls of the left ventricle.
options.D: It controls the electrical rhythm of the heart valves.

explanation: Spot on! The LAD feeds the thick, heavy-duty walls of the left ventricle. If it gets blocked, the heart's main pumping power is severely crippled.

question: Which type of nursing standard focuses directly on the environment and available resources?

options.A: Financial standards
options.B: Structure standards
options.C: Process standards
options.D: Outcome standards

explanation: Structure standards look at the physical setup, tools, and staffing numbers needed before care even begins. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h2)

question: Why must a nurse make sure a patient takes off any metal jewelry before an X-ray?

options.A: Metal items will permanently ruin the X-ray film
options.B: Metal objects block the rays and create artifacts
options.C: Metal interferes with the magnetic field used
options.D: Metal can absorb radiation and burn the skin

explanation: Metal blocks X-rays completely, leaving bright white spots on the image. These spots can hide fractures, so taking off jewelry or metal items is a quick safety step you won't want to miss.

question: Why is it so helpful to check a patient's diet early on?

options.A: Predicting future genetic mutations in children
options.B: Determining the exact date of hospital discharge
options.C: Detecting nutrient deficiencies before physical signs appear
options.D: Calculating the financial cost of grocery shopping

explanation: Spotting nutrition problems early means you can jump in and help before things get worse. Excellent nursing intuition!

question: What is the most important thing to check on a mother right after she delivers?

options.A: Visual acuity and hearing reflex responses
options.B: Uterine tone and amount of vaginal bleeding
options.C: Serum electrolyte levels and kidney function
options.D: Bowel motility and digestive enzyme output

explanation: Safety first! Checking that the uterus feels firm and watching the bleeding amount helps you catch heavy postpartum bleeding early.

question: A patient presents to the clinic reporting stool coming through her vagina two weeks after a difficult childbirth. What is the nurse's priority action during assessment?

options.A: Tell the patient this is a normal postpartum change that will resolve in a few days
options.B: Provide a gentle, empathetic history and prepare the patient for a careful physical examination
options.C: Perform a high-pressure enema to clear the bowel immediately
options.D: Immediately schedule the patient for emergency major surgery without further assessment

explanation: A sensitive history and gentle physical examination are essential to confirm the diagnosis and assess tissue health before planning treatment. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h4)

question: How should an accountable leader react when a serious clinical error happens on their ward?

options.A: Pretend the event never happened to protect the hospital's image
options.B: Hide the incident report so no one else finds out about it
options.C: Punish the entire nursing shift immediately without investigating
options.D: Use the mistake as an opportunity for systemic review and learning

explanation: Blaming people doesn't stop future errors. Accountable leaders look at the bigger picture to see what in the system failed, turning mistakes into valuable lessons.

question: Why do babies with chlamydial eye infections usually need treatment that goes through the whole body (systemic), not just eye drops?

options.A: Eye drops are too painful for a newborn to tolerate
options.B: Oral medications work faster than eye drops
options.C: Topical eye drops alone cannot clear the systemic infection
options.D: Systemic drugs prevent the development of fever

explanation: You nailed it! Chlamydia doesn't just hang out in the eye; it can hide in other areas like the throat, meaning oral or systemic meds are needed to fully kick it.

question: A student looks at a slide where bone-building cells (osteoblasts) are laying down matrix directly into a tissue sheet. What process is happening?

options.A: Intramembranous ossification
options.B: Interstitial bone growth
options.C: Endochondral ossification
options.D: Articular cartilage repair

explanation: Spot on! When bone forms straight from a connective tissue sheet without a cartilage stage, it's called intramembranous ossification.

question: Which of the following is a healthy, adaptive way to cope with stress?

options.A: Denying that any problem or difficulty exists at all
options.B: Isolating oneself completely from family and friends
options.C: Seeking social support and practicing deep breathing
options.D: Using heavy alcohol consumption to forget problems

explanation: Reaching out to loved ones and doing breathing exercises help calm your nervous system without creating extra problems.

question: Why are heart muscle cells branched instead of straight?

options.A: To connect with multiple neighboring cells and form a synchronized network
options.B: To allow the heart to store extra glycogen reserves
options.C: To increase the speed of nerve impulse transmission from the brain
options.D: To prevent the heart muscle from undergoing aerobic respiration

explanation: Think of it like a handshake network! Branching helps every single cell link up with its neighbors so the whole heart can beat smoothly and together.

question: What does milking a drainage tube involve?

options.A: Disconnecting the drainage bag completely and washing the inside with soap
options.B: Injecting large volumes of sterile water upward into the wound site
options.C: Twisting the tube tightly until the fluid stops flowing completely
options.D: Gently squeezing and releasing the tubing downward to push clots along

explanation: Milking is a gentle technique used to clear minor blockages by compressing the tubing progressively toward the collection container. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h3)

question: Why must a nurse remember that not every large or palpable mass in the genitourinary area is cancer?

options.A: Non-cancerous conditions like BPH can also create large, feelable masses
options.B: Malignant tumors are impossible to feel during a physical exam
options.C: Palpable masses are only ever caused by trapped fluid pockets
options.D: Benign growths always shrink on their own without any treatment

explanation: Conditions like benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) can make an organ swell up big enough to feel during an exam, which is why doctors always order tests like biopsies to be sure.

question: When scrubbing and rinsing your arms, which direction should you always go?

options.A: Beginning at your upper arm and moving down
options.B: From your elbows down toward your fingertips
options.C: Starting at your wrists and moving in circles
options.D: From your fingertips up toward your elbows

explanation: Always move from the cleanest part (fingertips) to the less clean part (elbows). Easy to remember!

question: What is the main difference between common cause variation and special cause variation?

options.A: Common cause requires a query, while special cause can be completely ignored.
options.B: Common cause is fully preventable, while special cause is impossible to track.
options.C: Common cause only happens at night, while special cause happens in the morning.
options.D: Common cause is expected and normal, while special cause comes from unusual, unexpected events.

explanation: Common causes are the everyday bumps in the road, while special causes are rare, unexpected surprises that need a closer look.

question: Where is the best anatomical site to inject emergency epinephrine?

options.A: Gluteal muscle
options.B: Mid-outer thigh
options.C: Subcutaneous abdomen
options.D: Deltoid muscle

explanation: The vastus lateralis (mid-outer thigh) absorbs epinephrine the fastest into the bloodstream. Plus, you can even give it right through trousers in a rush!

question: What is the main purpose of using Microsoft PowerPoint in healthcare?

options.A: Tracking daily financial budgets and supply inventories
options.B: Creating visual presentations for education and meetings
options.C: Writing formal legal contracts and employment policies
options.D: Storing confidential patient diagnostic test results

explanation: PowerPoint is your best friend for teaching! It helps you put together engaging slides for class presentations and health talks. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h4)

question: What usually happens to public health funding when the national economy goes through a tough patch?

options.A: Private clinics take over all public patients
options.B: Hospitals receive a sudden surge of extra grants
options.C: The cost of medical care drops to zero everywhere
options.D: Government health budgets are often reduced

explanation: Spot on. When money is tight nationally, governments collect less revenue and unfortunately tend to slash public sector budgets, including healthcare.

question: Why are local drama and folk media effective strategies in community mobilisation?

options.A: They provide a strict legal punishment for people who ignore health advice
options.B: They communicate health messages using culturally familiar and engaging entertainment
options.C: They force the government to release emergency healthcare funds instantly
options.D: They replace the need for any professional medical staff in the clinic

explanation: Drama and songs capture attention and break down complex health ideas into relatable stories. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h6)

question: What key message should form the heart of community health campaigns against abusive widowhood rites?

options.A: Honoring the dead should never involve harming or degrading the living
options.B: Widows should relocate to foreign countries immediately after a loss
options.C: All traditional cultural practices in Africa must be completely abolished
options.D: Men should be subjected to the exact same mourning rituals

explanation: Focusing the message on respect for human life and dignity wins people over while clearly standing against dangerous rituals. Fantastic job completing this set!

question: What do we call the breathing difficulty that gets worse when a patient lies flat?

options.A: Sudden breathlessness that occurs only at noon
options.B: Inability to speak full sentences due to pain
options.C: Breathlessness that worsens when lying flat
options.D: Shortness of breath triggered by cold air

explanation: That's orthopnoea! Patients naturally prop themselves up with pillows to catch their breath. You will see this often in heart failure cases.

question: How does a nurse manager apply systems thinking when a drug dose is missed on the ward?

options.A: By investigating the design of the drug chart, handovers, and dispensing process
options.B: By telling everyone to work twice as hard
options.C: By ignoring it if the patient seems fine
options.D: By immediately suspending the nurse who had the busiest shift

explanation: Instead of blaming the individual, a good leader checks if the process itself set the nurse up to struggle.

question: You notice raw, red skin inside a patient's nostrils while getting ready to put on a nasal cannula. What should you do first?

options.A: Scrub the irritated skin vigorously with an antiseptic alcohol wipe
options.B: Switch the patient immediately to an invasive mechanical ventilator
options.C: Refuse to start the oxygen therapy until the skin is completely healed
options.D: Document the finding, apply a water-based lubricant if ordered, and monitor the area closely

explanation: Always check and document skin status! Protecting sore areas with safe, water-based lubricants helps prevent further friction without stopping vital oxygen.

question: As a community nurse, you teach villagers to clear stagnant water around their homes to stop mosquitoes. Which part of the epidemiological triangle are you targeting?

options.A: The human host
options.B: The clinical symptoms
options.C: The environment
options.D: The infectious agent

explanation: Exactly! Clearing stagnant water changes the external environment to take away breeding sites for the mosquitoes.

question: What does it mean if a symptom shows up long after the normal incubation window has passed?

options.A: The patient's immune system is too perfect
options.B: The disease has been totally cured by magic
options.C: The laboratory test results are always wrong
options.D: It points to a different sickness or a newer exposure

explanation: When the timeline doesn't fit standard patterns, nurses should suspect a different illness or that the patient picked up the bug a second time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T84#GNS214_U1_T84_h4)

question: How should a nurse handle cultural beliefs when teaching teenagers about reproductive health?

options.A: Delay all care until the client reaches the age of twenty-one
options.B: Balance cultural sensitivity with evidence-based health education and safety
options.C: Ignore community norms completely and lecture parents on backward customs
options.D: Refuse to provide any counseling to avoid angering community elders

explanation: You've got this! A great nurse respects community traditions while making sure young clients still get accurate, lifesaving health information. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h7)

question: In males, which organ sits right below the bladder and wraps around the urethra?

options.A: The epididymis
options.B: The prostate gland
options.C: The testicle
options.D: The seminal vesicle

explanation: The prostate gland wraps like a ring around the upper male urethra. This is why an enlarged prostate in older men can make it hard to pass urine!

question: Why is a subgaleal hemorrhage considered a life-threatening emergency in a newborn?

options.A: It causes immediate respiratory arrest
options.B: It dissolves the cranial bones completely
options.C: It always results in permanent facial paralysis
options.D: It holds enough blood to cause severe shock

explanation: The large potential space beneath the galea aponeurosis can accumulate a massive amount of blood, leading to rapid hypovolemia and shock. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h3)

question: What is a common myth about teaching young people about sexual health?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for primary healthcare clinics
options.B: It is illegal under all international human rights laws
options.C: It causes severe physical side effects in teenagers
options.D: It encourages promiscuity and early sexual activity

explanation: Exactly! Many people wrongly fear that talking about sex encourages it, but studies show education actually helps youth make safer choices and wait longer.

question: Why do daily wage earners find it difficult to attend primary healthcare clinics during the day?

options.A: Clinics refuse to treat people who work in the informal sector
options.B: Transportation is completely unavailable during daytime hours
options.C: Doctors only consult patients during the night
options.D: They lose a day of critical income while waiting at the hospital

explanation: Long daytime waiting hours present a direct financial penalty for men who depend on daily wages to survive. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal complication of being unconscious and immobile for a long time?

options.A: Muscle contractures and joint stiffness
options.B: Deep vein thrombosis in the lower legs
options.C: Pressure ulcers on bony prominences
options.D: Rapid spontaneous recovery of cognitive speech

explanation: You got it! Prolonged unconsciousness causes physical problems like blood clots and stiff joints, rather than a sudden, magical recovery of speech.

question: What is the correct action a nurse should take before applying a new dose of a topical skin cream?

options.A: Shave all body hair from the area regardless of the medication type
options.B: Scrub the skin hard with alcohol wipes to remove the stratum corneum
options.C: Gently clean the skin to remove old medication residue and dirt
options.D: Apply a thick layer of plastic wrap over the old cream without cleaning

explanation: Cleaning away old residue and debris ensures proper contact and prevents chemical buildup or irritation on the skin surface. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h6)

question: A nurse in a busy rural clinic runs out of sterile gloves during an emergency wound dressing. What is the safest clinical action?

options.A: Obtain fresh supplies or use available clean alternatives according to protocol, avoiding unsafe shortcuts
options.B: Cancel the procedure and send the patient home without care
options.C: Perform the procedure barehanded to save time
options.D: Reuse a discarded pair of gloves after washing them with cold water

explanation: Shortages should never excuse compromising basic safety; nurses must secure proper supplies or follow approved institutional alternatives. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h2)

question: Which family planning supply method gives dual protection against BOTH pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Male condoms
options.B: Oral contraceptive pills
options.C: Spermicidal creams
options.D: Cervical caps

explanation: Condoms act as a physical shield that blocks body fluids, stopping both conception and many infections at once. Smart nursing knowledge!

question: Why does a shortened fallopian tube raise the risk of an ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: The fertilized egg implants inside the tube before reaching the uterus
options.B: Ovaries release eggs directly into the abdominal wall
options.C: Tubal smooth muscle completely loses its ability to contract
options.D: Sperm travel too slowly to reach the ampulla in time

explanation: Since the egg moves too fast and doesn't time its journey right, it can end up planting itself inside the tiny wall of the fallopian tube instead of the uterus.

question: What is the medical term for the physical act of swallowing?

options.A: Mastication
options.B: Deglutition
options.C: Peristalsis
options.D: Aspiration

explanation: Deglutition is the formal medical word for swallowing, covering both the voluntary and involuntary phases of moving food down. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why is a patient in the prodromal stage often a high risk for spreading germs to others?

options.A: Their immune system has completely stopped functioning
options.B: They feel well enough to move around while carrying germs
options.C: They shed the highest volume of toxic waste products
options.D: Pathogens multiply exclusively during this specific phase

explanation: Spot on! Because they don't feel super sick yet, they keep moving around and unknowingly expose people around them.

question: Which of these can act as a reservoir where germs live?

options.A: Completely dry and sunny metal surfaces
options.B: Sterile surgical instruments only
options.C: Soil, water, humans, and animals
options.D: Intact human skin with no normal flora

explanation: Germs aren't picky! They can live inside living hosts like humans and animals, or in the environment like soil and water.

question: A patient with rapid-acting insulin asks when they should take their injection. What is the best nursing advice?

options.A: Only right before going to sleep at night
options.B: Just before or right at mealtime
options.C: Two hours after finishing the meal
options.D: Once a week on an empty stomach

explanation: Rapid-acting insulin starts working very quickly, so patients take it right as they eat to match the incoming food sugars. Spot on!

question: What is the best and simplest guide for a nursing mother on how much fluid to drink?

options.A: Drink fluids whenever she feels thirsty
options.B: Avoid all liquids for two hours after each feeding
options.C: Drink only carbonated soft drinks to stay energized
options.D: Force herself to drink ten liters daily regardless of thirst

explanation: Your body's natural thirst cue is a fantastic guide during lactation. Drinking a glass of water during each nursing session is a wonderful habit to build.

question: What is the main goal of having both the sympathetic and parasympathetic systems working together?

options.A: Maintaining a stable internal body balance
options.B: Preventing the brain from ever sleeping
options.C: Keeping the heart rate as high as possible
options.D: Ensuring constant physical exhaustion

explanation: Both systems balance each other out to achieve homeostasis—a fancy word for keeping your internal body happy, stable, and healthy. Brilliant work!

question: Why is achieving small, quick wins important when dealing with a resistant community?

options.A: It allows the nurse to take an extended holiday leave
options.B: It proves that traditional leaders have no real authority
options.C: It forces the local government to increase health sector taxes
options.D: It helps restore faith and revive interest in the health system

explanation: Tangible, early successes demonstrate competence and genuine commitment, helping to break down skepticism and resistance. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h6)

question: When is the best time to put a newborn baby to the breast for the very first time?

options.A: Only when the mother's milk turns white
options.B: After twenty-four hours of observation
options.C: Within the first hour after birth
options.D: Once the baby cries continuously

explanation: You nailed it! Starting breastfeeding within that first hour helps boost milk flow and gives the baby that precious, protective colostrum.

question: What is the main use of a family planning client register in the clinic?

options.A: To record detailed client information and services given sequentially
options.B: To track daily weather patterns affecting clinic attendance
options.C: To advertise new contraceptive brands to visiting community members
options.D: To list the financial debts owed by the local health facility

explanation: Great thinking! The client register keeps a neat, step-by-step history of everyone who visits for family planning care.

question: Why is empowering women through education considered a key objective within population policies?

options.A: It ensures women never participate in agricultural activities.
options.B: It forces families to move permanently to urban centers.
options.C: It eliminates the need for any maternal healthcare clinics.
options.D: It naturally influences family size choices and improves overall health.

explanation: Education is a game-changer! When women are educated, they often choose to marry a bit later, seek out better healthcare, and freely decide on family sizes that work best for them.

question: What is the benefit of using standardized referral proformas in mental health care?

options.A: They ensure that all essential clinical and historical data is consistently recorded
options.B: They automatically guarantee financial sponsorship for the client
options.C: They eliminate the need for nurses to speak with clients or families
options.D: They prevent tertiary hospitals from ever discharging clients back home

explanation: Using standard referral forms makes sure no important medical or social history gets accidentally left out.

question: How do out-of-pocket purchases by patients for basic ward supplies affect hospital records?

options.A: They distort standard cost calculations because items are bought outside the system
options.B: They guarantee that all indirect costs are fully covered by the government
options.C: They make hospital accounting completely automatic and error-free
options.D: They eliminate the need for patient classification systems

explanation: When patients run out to buy their own routine supplies, the hospital's official records miss the true picture of what delivering care actually costs.

question: How does Rifampicin stop TB bacteria from multiplying?

options.A: By dissolving the patient's lung tissue
options.B: By inhibiting bacterial RNA synthesis
options.C: By destroying the human liver cells
options.D: By blocking human vitamin absorption

explanation: Rifampicin targets bacterial RNA synthesis, halting the germ's ability to make essential proteins and grow.

question: Why are modern hospitals moving away from just blaming individuals when mistakes happen?

options.A: Because fixing underlying system flaws prevents future errors better
options.B: Because hospital management no longer cares about errors
options.C: Because nurses refuse to complete incident reports
options.D: Because punishing workers stops all future mistakes

explanation: Looking at system problems instead of just pointing fingers helps fix the root cause so the same mistake doesn't happen again. Great nursing practice starts with understanding this!

question: What happens during the action and implementation phase?

options.A: A new set of leaders is elected to replace the old chiefs
options.B: The community votes to cancel the project due to high costs
options.C: Health workers sit in an office and write final reports
options.D: The plans created by the community are put into actual practice

explanation: Implementation is the doing phase where the agreed-upon activities, like clearing brush or building facilities, are carried out. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h6)

question: If a patient scrapes the surface of their skin without a deep cut, which layer took the hit?

options.A: Subcutaneous fat layer
options.B: Skeletal muscle
options.C: Hypodermis
options.D: Stratum corneum

explanation: Correct! The stratum corneum is the very top layer of the epidermis, meaning it handles all the daily friction and minor scrapes. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which type of exercise involves the nurse moving the joints of a patient who cannot move at all?

options.A: Passive exercises
options.B: Resistive exercises
options.C: Active exercises
options.D: Active-assistive exercises

explanation: When a patient cannot move their limbs themselves, you step in and gently move their joints for them. That is what passive exercises are all about!

question: What is the first thing a nurse should do right after a shock is delivered?

options.A: Resume chest compressions right away
options.B: Administer a routine dose of IV atropine
options.C: Draw blood samples for arterial blood gas analysis
options.D: Check the carotid pulse for up to one minute

explanation: Don't pause to check for a pulse immediately! Modern resuscitation rules tell us to jump right back into chest compressions to keep blood flowing.

question: What is the correct order for putting on (donning) your PPE before entering an isolation room?

options.A: Mask first, then gloves, gown, and eye protection
options.B: Gloves first, then gown, mask, and protective eyewear
options.C: Eye protection first, followed by gloves, gown, and mask
options.D: Gown first, then mask or respirator, eye protection, and gloves

explanation: Great job! You start by covering your body with the gown, secure your breathing and eyes, and pull your glove cuffs over the gown sleeves last so there are no skin gaps.

question: Why are folk media like traditional drama and local songs so effective in rural communities?

options.A: They require expensive electronic equipment and stable electricity to function
options.B: They focus strictly on complex medical terminology and research data
options.C: They eliminate the need for nurses to speak to the community directly
options.D: They connect deeply with local culture and engage audiences who may not read well

explanation: Using familiar cultural practices makes health messages fun and accessible to everyone in the community, regardless of literacy.

question: Why is a physical head-to-toe check important during a nutrition assessment?

options.A: It calculates the precise daily caloric expenditure during rest
options.B: It reveals visible deficiency signs like swollen gums or pale skin
options.C: It replaces the need for laboratory blood tests and dietary records
options.D: It accurately measures the exact percentage of body water volume

explanation: By simply looking at a patient's hair, skin, eyes, and mouth, you can often spot early physical clues of missing vitamins and minerals.

question: What does an anterior body landmark refer to?

options.A: A structure located on the front of the body
options.B: A structure located on the back of the body
options.C: A bony prominence found only on the skull
options.D: A deep internal organ with no surface visibility

explanation: Anterior landmarks are situated on the front or ventral surface of the human body. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h5)

question: What was the main idea behind the moral treatment movement?

options.A: Spiritual exorcism is the only permanent cure for psychological distress
options.B: Medication is the sole effective intervention for mental disorders
options.C: Patients require strict physical restraint to prevent violent outbursts
options.D: Mental illness should be met with kindness, patience, and a peaceful environment

explanation: Moral treatment tossed out cruelty and punishment. Instead, it focused on human dignity, fresh air, useful activities, and gentle care from staff.

question: What is the medical term used when a patient's bad reaction stops after the suspected drug is withdrawn?

options.A: Tolerance
options.B: Anaphylaxis
options.C: Dechallenge
options.D: Rechallenge

explanation: Think of 'dechallenge' as un-challenging the body—stopping the medicine to see if the symptoms get better or go away.

question: A patient gets a painkiller derived from the opium poppy after surgery. Which drug is it?

options.A: Quinine
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Morphine
options.D: Digoxin

explanation: Morphine is a powerful pain-relieving medication extracted right from the opium poppy plant. You'll see this often in clinicals!

question: What is the best first step a nurse should take when suspecting a patient is experiencing abuse?

options.A: Wait until the patient voluntarily brings up the assault during discharge
options.B: Provide a private, confidential setting before asking gentle screening questions
options.C: Immediately call local law enforcement to arrest everyone in the waiting room
options.D: Loudly demand details about the perpetrator in front of waiting family members

explanation: Privacy and a safe, non-judgmental space are everything. It helps the patient feel secure enough to trust you.

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to nursing audits in many Nigerian healthcare facilities?

options.A: Severe shortage of nursing staff and high workloads
options.B: Fear of victimization among junior nursing staff
options.C: Excessive availability of fully automated robotic wards
options.D: Heavy reliance on physical, paper-based case notes

options.C: To build team readiness and ensure a smooth emergency response
options.D: To accurately predict the exact calendar date of the next natural disaster

explanation: Practice makes perfect! Drills help staff know their roles inside out, cutting down panic when a real emergency hits.

question: Why do boat nurses need a wide, general set of nursing skills?

options.A: Cruise ship passengers only experience minor travel fatigue.
options.B: They often work alone or with a tiny team and must handle many different health issues.
options.C: They rotate through different land hospitals every single week.
options.D: Maritime law requires them to specialize in surgery and pediatrics.

explanation: You got it! Because specialists are rarely onboard, these nurses must be ready to independently handle anything from a simple tummy ache to sudden injuries.

question: A relative panics after noticing strange, irregular breathing patterns in a dying patient. How do you respond?

options.A: Confirm that the patient is in severe, unmanaged pain
options.B: Immediately start emergency cardiopulmonary resuscitation
options.C: Tell the relative to leave the room until breathing normalizes
options.D: Explain that changing breathing patterns are a normal part of dying

explanation: Giving a calm heads-up about changes like Cheyne-Stokes breathing helps soothe the family's fears during those final hours.

question: What does a pulse oximeter actually measure in the patient?

options.A: Exact blood pressure inside the artery
options.B: Total red blood cell count in the body
options.C: Oxygen saturation percentage in the blood
options.D: Carbon dioxide levels in the lungs

explanation: The device uses light absorption to estimate how much hemoglobin is carrying oxygen. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h2)

question: How does a vision statement differ from a mission statement?

options.A: A vision statement is created by junior staff, while a mission is written by the government
options.B: A vision statement looks forward to future aspirations, while a mission focuses on present purpose
options.C: A vision statement is kept secret from patients, while a mission is printed on posters
options.D: A vision statement deals strictly with daily nursing chores, while a mission covers finances

explanation: Visions describe a future desired state, whereas missions focus on what the organization is doing today. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h2)

question: What makes an event count as a natural disaster in healthcare?

options.A: Any medical emergency involving more than ten patients at once
options.B: A minor incident managed easily by standard daily staffing
options.C: An event that overwhelms local healthcare and community resources
options.D: An accident that occurs only within a hospital or clinic setting

explanation: A natural disaster is marked by its ability to stretch local resources past their breaking point, meaning outside help is needed to handle the health crisis. You've got this!

question: What does the term 'orthostatic hypotension' mean?

options.A: A sudden drop in blood pressure when standing up
options.B: Swelling in the lower legs due to poor circulation
options.C: A spike in heart rate after eating heavy meals
options.D: High blood pressure caused by sleeping flat on the back

explanation: When blood vessels are slow to adjust to a new position, standing up too fast can cause a dizzy spell because of a sudden drop in pressure. Good to know for patient safety!

question: A patient shows you a skin mole that has recently changed color and grown irregularly. What should you do first?

options.A: Refer the patient for a prompt medical evaluation and biopsy.
options.B: Advise the patient to monitor the mole at home for another year.
options.C: Apply a medicated topical steroid cream to mole.
options.D: Reassure the patient that changing moles are always benign.

explanation: Any changing mole or spot needs a professional check-up right away to rule out skin cancer. You are learning to protect your patients!

question: What is the correct hand motion on the push rims when a patient is moving a manual wheelchair forward?

options.A: Grip at ten o'clock and push forward down to two o'clock
options.B: Grab the top of the wheels and pull backward continuously
options.C: Smack the spokes of the wheels with an open palm
options.D: Hold the hand rims tightly still while kicking the floor

explanation: Starting at ten o'clock gives the best mechanical advantage and long stroke length for efficient forward motion. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h5)

question: Why is fast teamwork among healthcare staff so essential when managing GI complications?

options.A: Conditions can deteriorate into life-threatening emergencies very quickly
options.B: Nurses are not allowed to touch patients without a doctor present
options.C: Medical staff must share paperwork equally among themselves
options.D: Collaborative care guarantees that surgery will never be needed

explanation: You got it! Emergencies like bowel tears or massive bleeding move fast, meaning the team has to act together instantly to keep the patient safe. Teamwork makes the dream work in nursing!

question: What do we call nutrients that our bodies cannot make on their own, so we must get them from our food?

options.A: Secondary metabolites
options.B: Synthetic polymers
options.C: Endogenous proteins
options.D: Essential nutrients

explanation: Spot on! Essential nutrients are the ones your body can't manufacture by itself, so eating them is a must for survival.

question: Why do large hospitals rely heavily on computer servers?

options.A: To replace human nurses during night shifts
options.B: To automatically inject medications into IV lines
options.C: To print out every single patient chart on paper
options.D: To store electronic health records and manage hospital network traffic centrally

explanation: Servers are powerful central computers that keep all hospital records safe and connect computers across different wards.

question: When a patient is newly connected to a ventilator, what is the most common starting PEEP (Positive End-Expiratory Pressure) setting used to keep small air sacs open?

options.A: 20 cmH2O
options.B: 5 cmH2O
options.C: 0 cmH2O
options.D: 50 cmH2O

explanation: A baseline PEEP of 5 cmH2O acts like a gentle cushion at the end of each breath, stopping tiny air sacs (alveoli) from collapsing so breathing stays easier.

question: Why is herd immunity so helpful for vulnerable people in a community?

options.A: It guarantees that every single person in the population will develop permanent natural immunity
options.B: It completely eliminates all known environmental reservoirs of a bacterial pathogen
options.C: It transforms live vaccines into safer, non-replicating subunit vaccines
options.D: It reduces overall disease spread, indirectly protecting those who cannot be vaccinated

explanation: Brilliant! When most people are vaccinated, germs struggle to spread, keeping even the unvaccinated safe.

question: A nurse leading a polio vaccination campaign notices sudden community resistance due to false rumors spread on social media. What is the best immediate response?

options.A: Punish any community member who asks questions about the vaccine
options.B: Engage trusted community leaders to openly address and debunk the rumors
options.C: Ignore the rumors completely and hope the villagers forget them
options.D: Cancel the entire vaccination campaign and close the health clinic

explanation: Rumors spread fast, but trusted local voices spread clarity faster! Partnering with community leaders is the best way to calm fears and protect public health.

question: What is the main goal of community mobilisation in primary health care?

options.A: Empowering locals to take charge of health
options.B: Replacing traditional healers with doctors
options.C: Relying entirely on government funding
options.D: Imposing foreign medical standards

explanation: Community mobilisation focuses on enabling local populations to identify and solve their own health problems. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h1)

question: What is a major risk when relying only on written charts during an audit?

options.A: Patients will refuse to take their prescribed hospital medications
options.B: Doctors will take over all the responsibilities of the nursing staff
options.C: Care might have been given but simply not documented by the nurse
options.D: Case notes might turn into digital files without any human input

explanation: Exactly! Heavy workloads on the ward sometimes mean a nurse performed a procedure wonderfully, but was simply too busy to write it down.

question: On the Braden Scale, what does a lower score tell you about a patient?

options.A: Immediate need for a fall prevention program
options.B: Higher risk for developing pressure injuries
options.C: Lower risk for developing pressure injuries
options.D: Excellent skin integrity and high mobility

explanation: You're doing great! On the Braden Scale, lower numbers mean the patient's skin is more vulnerable, so they need extra care and frequent turning.

question: What is the absolute first action a nurse expects when caring for a patient with serum sickness?

options.A: Stop administering the triggering medication
options.B: Start immediate daily kidney dialysis
options.C: Give a blood transfusion to replace red cells
options.D: Apply cool water compresses to the joints

explanation: Rule number one in pharmacology reactions: stop the offending drug immediately so no more immune complexes can form!

question: Why is yellow jaundice showing up in the first 24 hours of life a worry for nurses?

options.A: It indicates that the mother is breastfeeding too frequently
options.B: It is a normal physiological process seen in all preterm babies
options.C: It shows that the infant is experiencing acute dehydration
options.D: It points to pathological processes like blood group incompatibility

explanation: Jaundice on day one is never normal. While regular newborn jaundice can show up later, early jaundice usually means something serious like blood type mismatch or liver trouble.

question: A community health nurse is teaching a mother how to improve her family's protein intake using affordable local foods. What is the best advice?

options.A: Combine local plant sources like beans and maize to get complete proteins
options.B: Feed the family exclusively imported vitamin pills instead of meals
options.C: Avoid all local staple carbohydrates like yam and cassava completely
options.D: Rely only on expensive red meat imported from overseas

explanation: Pairing local plant foods like beans and maize gives you a complete protein combo without breaking the bank. Brilliant nursing care!

question: Which of the following conditions is a classic example of a metabolic crisis in diabetes?

options.A: Prolonged hypoglycemia
options.B: Diabetic ketoacidosis
options.C: Diabetic neuropathy
options.D: Chronic foot ulceration

explanation: Diabetic ketoacidosis is an acute, life-threatening metabolic emergency caused by severe insulin deficiency and acid buildup. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a right that patients keep while on psychiatric parole?

options.A: The right to completely ignore court-ordered treatment without consequences
options.B: The right to give informed consent for general healthcare
options.C: The right to access legal help and representation
options.D: The right to be treated with dignity and professional respect

explanation: You nailed it! Parole comes with conditions—ignoring your treatment plan means breaking those conditions, which leads back to clinical or legal intervention.

question: What is a tough ethical situation a home-birth midwife might face during an emergency?

options.A: A client refusing a recommended transfer to a hospital facility
options.B: Deciding which brand of delivery gloves to purchase
options.C: Having too many medical doctors volunteering at a home birth
options.D: Complaining about the weather conditions during labor

explanation: It's a tricky balance! You must respect a patient's choices, but your clinical duty is to keep mom and baby safe when danger arises.

question: During a community disease outbreak, what is the main cause of biological hazard emergencies?

options.A: Accidental leakage of industrial gas from factories
options.B: Sudden heavy rainfall flooding residential areas
options.C: Rapid spread of infectious diseases among populations
options.D: Widespread consumption of expired tinned foods

explanation: Biological hazards are living microscopic troublemakers like bacteria and viruses that spread fast through communities. Keep up the good work!

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for triggering the milk ejection or let-down reflex during breastfeeding?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Oxytocin causes the tiny muscles around the milk glands to squeeze, pushing the milk down the ducts so the baby can drink it easily. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h1)

question: What is the primary focus of accident prevention in nursing care?

options.A: Strict bedrest enforcement
options.B: Expensive home renovations
options.C: Proactive risk identification
options.D: Punishing careless behaviors

explanation: Nurses focus heavily on finding and fixing hazards before an actual injury happens to the patient. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h1)

question: A nurse is checking a patient with early liver failure for brain confusion. Which physical sign should she look for?

options.A: Sudden paralysis of the lower extremities
options.B: Involuntary flapping tremor of the hands (asterixis)
options.C: Rigid muscle spasms in the jaw
options.D: Inability to focus the eyes on bright objects

explanation: Asterixis (often called a 'liver flap') is a classic sign where the patient holds their hands out, and the wrists briefly flap downward due to toxin buildup.

question: What is the main drawback of using a 24-hour dietary recall?

options.A: It requires expensive laboratory equipment
options.B: It relies heavily on the patient's memory
options.C: It measures blood chemistry instead of food
options.D: It takes months to complete and analyze

explanation: People easily forget what they ate yesterday, which can lead to a few blank spots in a 24-hour recall!

question: In the classic ABCD HIV prevention strategy, what does the letter 'C' stand for?

options.A: Care coordination
options.B: CD4 counting
options.C: Condom use
options.D: Clinical cure

explanation: That's right! 'C' stands for consistent condom use, which blocks the exchange of infectious body fluids during sex.

question: Why do very busy hospital wards sometimes lead to unsafe injection practices?

options.A: High patient loads and supply limits tempt staff to rush or cut corners
options.B: New nursing graduates are rarely taught basic injection techniques
options.C: Modern equipment requires electricity that is often unstable
options.D: Patients demand faster injections when waiting rooms are crowded

explanation: True story in many clinics: when resources are tight and too many patients are waiting, pressure mounts. But remember, we must never let stress push us into dangerous shortcuts like reusing gear.

question: Which international declaration in 1978 made Primary Health Care the main strategy for global health?

options.A: The Alma-Ata Declaration
options.B: The Geneva Nursing Charter
options.C: The Lagos Health Accord
options.D: The London Sanitary Treaty

explanation: Remember Alma-Ata! The 1978 conference put Primary Health Care on the map as the key to health for everyone.

question: What do vitamins A, C, and E mainly do for your skin?

options.A: Increasing the overall thickness of the subcutaneous fat layer
options.B: Acting as primary cleansers for the epidermal surface
options.C: Directly producing melanin to determine skin color
options.D: Acting as antioxidants to protect cells from oxidative stress

explanation: Spot on! These vitamins act like little bodyguards, fighting off nasty molecules that try to damage your skin cells.

question: How does expanding mandatory health insurance help solve healthcare financing problems?

options.A: It creates a reliable, pooled fund that reduces financial barriers for patients
options.B: It allows doctors to set their own salaries without government review
options.C: It forces international donors to double their annual monetary grants
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for primary healthcare centers

explanation: Brilliant! Mandatory insurance keeps a steady flow of money coming into hospitals while saving everyday people from sudden, crushing medical bills.

question: How do strict professional hierarchies sometimes hurt patient care?

options.A: They discourage junior staff and nurses from sharing critical patient observations
options.B: They ensure that every single medication is administered twice as fast
options.C: They eliminate all forms of communication errors between departments
options.D: They force patients to pay less money for hospital admission fees

explanation: Spot on! When junior staff or nurses feel intimidated by strict ranks, they might hold back life-saving observations out of fear.

question: Why is it important for a research paper to include a section about its own limitations?

options.A: It proves that the researchers spent a lot of money conducting the study
options.B: It ensures that other scientists never try to research that topic again
options.C: It shows honesty about potential flaws and stops readers from overgeneralizing conclusions
options.D: It gives the journal editors an excuse to reject the paper before publication

explanation: No study is 100% perfect. Admitting limitations helps other clinicians know where the findings might fall short so they don't overstate the results.

question: What is an important nursing action after giving an antagonist antidote like naloxone?

options.A: Placing the patient on a strict low-sodium hospital diet immediately
options.B: Checking the patient's deep tendon reflexes every six hours
options.C: Monitoring vital signs closely for sudden withdrawal or rebound effects
options.D: Discontinuing all intravenous fluids to prevent fluid overload

explanation: When you reverse an agonist too fast with an antagonist, the patient can suddenly experience intense withdrawal or symptoms roaring back. Always watch your patient closely!

question: What triggers the sarcoplasmic reticulum to release a flood of calcium inside a heart cell?

options.A: A small influx of extracellular calcium through membrane channels
options.B: The direct binding of ATP molecules to troponin C
options.C: The sudden drop in intracellular potassium levels
options.D: A massive flood of sodium ions directly from the T-tubules

explanation: It is a chain reaction! A little calcium trickles in from the outside, which triggers a much bigger release of stored calcium inside. Neat, right?

question: What is the primary focus of organisational objectives in healthcare?

options.A: The private business ventures of senior medical doctors
options.B: The daily social events organised by the nursing union
options.C: The personal retirement plans of individual staff members
options.D: The survival, growth, and overall service delivery of the institution

explanation: Organzational objectives look at the big picture—keeping the hospital running smoothly, growing, and providing great care to the community.

question: Why do nurses need to look at the whole picture—not just a single medical diagnosis—when caring for older adults?

options.A: Because doctors usually make mistakes when diagnosing elderly patients
options.B: Because patients only care about their emotional health
options.C: Because aging affects physical, mental, and social well-being simultaneously
options.D: Because chronic diseases disappear once the home environment is changed

explanation: You've got this! Older adults often face physical, emotional, and environmental challenges all at once. Looking at the big picture helps us give the best care possible.

question: What is the medical term for a resting heart rate that stays above 100 beats per minute?

options.A: Bradycardia
options.B: Asystole
options.C: Arrhythmia
options.D: Tachycardia

explanation: Tachy- means fast! So when a resting heart rate races above 100 beats per minute, we call it tachycardia.

question: Why is it helpful for nurses to know about different types of computers?

options.A: To know which device fits specific clinical and administrative tasks
options.B: To purchase personal computers for the hospital wards
options.C: To write programming codes for new hospital software systems
options.D: To be able to repair broken hardware components independently

explanation: Spot on! Different tasks need different tools—just like you wouldn't use a surgical blade to give an injection, you use the right computer (like a bedside tablet vs. a big office computer) for the job.

question: Which severe obstetric complication is frequently linked to early childbearing before the pelvis is fully developed?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Obstetric fistula
options.D: Chronic hypertension

explanation: Prolonged and obstructed labor in an immature pelvis creates abnormal holes between the birth canal and bladder or rectum, leading to continuous leakage. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h3)
